title: First run and the setup check
owns: the first-run and setup-check parts of app/renderer/home/** and the Start handling in main.ts (small hunk)

findings.title: On a Mac, fixing the only 'Fix' row hides the Setup check, with Screen Recording and Input Monitoring still unfixed, from the first-run window
findings.scenario: First launch on a Mac: Accessibility is a 'fail' (Fix), Screen Recording and Input Monitoring are 'warn' (Check). The consent text promises "macOS will ask you to allow Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring". Before Start, the Setup check is visible only because failing > 0. The user presses Open System Settings, allows Accessibility and returns; the window re-reads the status on focus, failing becomes 0, and `classList.toggle('after-setup', !failing)` hides the whole Setup section again (body.first-run hides .after-setup). The remaining Screen Recording and Input Monitoring buttons disappear, the tagline reverts to the generic 'Read how Ember works…', and the user can't finish granting before Start.
findings.evidence: Rendered with real inspectEnvironment() data for macOS in Chromium: initial first-run screenshot shows 'Setup check – 1 to fix' with three 'Open System Settings' buttons; after setting the accessibility check to ok and dispatching 'focus', the page text contains only the welcome card, picker and Start (no Setup check). Code: app/renderer/home/main.ts:214-217; app/main/environment.ts:267-285 (only accessibility is 'fail').
findings.fix: Keep the Setup section visible in first-run whenever any check is not ok (fail or warn) on macOS, or add a dedicated 'Allow Ember' step above Start listing Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring with their buttons. Tie the tagline to 'N permissions still to allow'.

findings.title: Start ignores the setup check: the window closes and Ember greets as if ready even when Accessibility, the helper or the session is unusable
findings.scenario: A Mac user with a gh sign-in (or any user whose Copilot connects) presses Start with Accessibility not allowed. settings.onChange -> settledPhase() -> phase 'ready' -> home.close() -> greet(): "I'll stay by your cursor. Press ⌃⇧⌘Space to ask me anything." The only permission surface (the Setup check, a collapsed fold near the bottom) closed with the window. The same happens on Linux with 'Screen reading: Accessibility is off' (RHEL 8's default, a warn), on Windows with 'Windows blocked Ember's accessibility helper' (warn, 'Unblock it') and on a Wayland session (fail). The README says 'its setup check says which are missing', but nothing brings the user there. macOS never prompts by itself either: Ember calls isTrustedAccessibilityClient(true), the one-pixel screen grab and CGRequestListenEventAccess only from the fix buttons. When the status says 'warn' the section is a closed fold labelled '1 to look at', the 'Setup' nav link has no badge, and the tagline says 'Press Win+Alt+Space to ask it anything.' (rendered). The handle says 'Ready' (idleWord looks only at Copilot).
findings.evidence: app/main/main.ts:1104-1121 (decision uses only phase); greet() at 436-456 ignores env checks; app/main/main.ts handle idle word from agent status only; rendered after-start-win-ready.png with a 'blocked-download' warn and Copilot ready: no hint of the warning above the fold; grep for accessibilityTrusted(prompt)/requestListenAccess shows no automatic call.
findings.fix: At first Start, if any check is fail or a capability-critical warn (macOS Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring; Linux Screen reading; Windows helper blocked), keep Settings open scrolled to Setup (as is already done for Copilot) and let greet() say what is missing. Add a count badge on the 'Setup' nav link, make the tagline mention open warns, and offer an 'Open settings' bubble action when a task can't read or capture.

findings.title: After the Linux 'Turn on' button the 'restart open apps' caveat disappears, and the README never mentions the switch
findings.scenario: On stock RHEL 8 (toolkit-accessibility false) the Setup check says 'Accessibility is off, so Ember can only see screenshots. Turn it on, then restart open apps.' with a Turn on button. After the click the row re-reads as OK: 'Accessibility is on', and the instruction is gone. The user asks Ember to act in a window opened earlier; Qt, Chromium and Firefox windows opened before the switch are not readable until restarted or the user logs out and in (docs/DEVELOPING.md:65, doctor.ts:138 'then log out and in'). Ember says it is ready. The README Linux section never mentions the switch.
findings.evidence: app/main/environment.ts:174-178; app/renderer/home/main.ts:195-200 (fix result just re-renders checks); app/main/doctor.ts:138 vs environment.ts:176 give different instructions ('log out and in' vs 'restart open apps').
findings.fix: After the fix, keep a note on the row ('On. Restart apps that were already open, or log out and in, so Ember can read them.') until the user dismisses it or the sidecar sees an app. Make the doctor and the setup check say the same thing, and add a line to the README's Linux install section.

findings.title: macOS 'Reset Ember's permissions' recovery is implemented but never offered; stale-grant recovery is a manual '−' and '+' instruction repeated on first run
findings.scenario: Every update replaces the ad-hoc signature, so macOS shows Ember switched on while the permission no longer applies (README says so). The only recovery shown is the sentence 'If Ember is already listed and switched on, remove it with − and add it again…', appended to the Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring and Microphone rows (and to every doctor row), including for a brand-new install where Ember is not listed yet. The designed one-click fix 'reset-permissions' (tccutil reset Accessibility/ScreenCapture/ListenEvent) exists in darwin/system/environment.ts but no check ever sets fix: 'reset-permissions' (nor 'open-automation-settings'), so it is dead code.
findings.evidence: grep -rn reset-permissions app: only the FixId type and darwin/system/environment.ts (RESET_SERVICES, label, apply); inspectMac() in app/main/environment.ts:267-285 never references it; rendered macOS Setup check shows the long sentence three times.
findings.fix: Offer 'Reset Ember's permissions' as a button on the Accessibility row when it fails after Ember was previously granted (or always as a secondary button). Show the '−/+' sentence only after the first Open System Settings press, or as one note under the list.

findings.title: 'Speak replies out loud' does nothing, with no message, when the system has no speech voice
findings.scenario: A RHEL 8 user (AppImage, or an install without the weak dependency speech-dispatcher-espeak-ng) turns on 'Speak replies, questions and results out loud'. Chromium's speechSynthesis finds no voice, onstart never fires, and nothing is heard. The settings window shows no error, because the 'Speaking' row exists only in the CLI doctor ('speech-dispatcher is missing…'), not in the Setup check. The user concludes speech is broken.
findings.evidence: app/renderer/mic/main.ts:61-72 (no onerror reporting, no voice check); app/main/doctor.ts speech row; app/main/environment.ts has no speech check; Voice.speak() at app/main/voice.ts only waits SPEECH_START_MS and gives up silently.
findings.fix: When speak() gets no onstart within the timeout (or getVoices() is empty), report it to main and show it under the 'Speak replies' switch and as a Setup check row with the OS fix (Linux: sudo dnf install speech-dispatcher speech-dispatcher-espeak-ng).

findings.title: First-run window: Start and the agree box are below the fold, and the copy points to sections that aren't shown yet and to features of other OSes
findings.scenario: At the default 760×640 window the first screen shows only the hero and the terms (rendered). The character picker, 'I've read how Ember works and I agree' and 'Start Ember' need a scroll that nothing hints at. The terms say 'turn on “Hey Ember” below' (the Voice section is hidden until Start), 'your never-look list' (the list is hidden too), and on macOS and Linux 'Ember can work in WSL', which is Windows-only (the WSL switch is hidden elsewhere). 'Accessibility service' is the only explanation of what Ember reads.
findings.evidence: Rendered first-run-win-640.png (Start below the fold); app/renderer/home/index.html:31-36; app/renderer/home/copy.ts homePatches doesn't patch these bullets per OS.
findings.fix: Put Start and agree in a sticky footer (or compact the terms); drop 'below' and 'never-look list' wording on first run; mention WSL only on Windows (patch via homePatches).

findings.title: Setup check and doctor wording: an unexplained warning, jargon labels and a dead-end 'Tell the Ember team'
findings.scenario: On RHEL 9, Fedora or Ubuntu the Setup check shows 'Check – Operating system – Ubuntu 22.04' with no reason (status warn, detail is just PRETTY_NAME; the README says RHEL 8 family only). The same Linux row is 'Screen reading' in Settings but 'Reading apps' in the doctor; the doctor also says 'Compositor', 'XTest', 'File watchers', 'Sandbox' to people who aren't admins, and on macOS lists both 'Microphone' ('Not checked here') and 'Microphone access'. The Windows 'Display scaling' warning ends 'Tell the Ember team.' with no address or link (the About section lists only a log file).
findings.evidence: app/main/environment.ts:139-145 and 241-243; app/main/doctor.ts labels (Reading apps, Compositor, Mouse and keyboard); app/main/platform/win32/system/doctor.ts / doctor.ts:helperRow; doctor output for macOS rendered via formatDoctor.
findings.fix: Add a reason to the OS warn ('Ember is tested on RHEL 8 and its family; this may work, but is not supported'), use one label per check in both surfaces, and give a concrete place to report problems (issue URL) in the About section and the 'Tell the Ember team' text.

findings.title: On a fresh macOS first run the headline already says “needs a couple of things fixed” and the Fix rows sit below Start
findings.scenario: Every new Mac user has Accessibility denied, so the check fails. The tagline then reads 'Ember needs a couple of things fixed before it can work on this machine.' instead of the first-run instruction 'Read how Ember works… then agree and press Start.' It says 'a couple' even for one item, uses 'machine' where the rest of the UI says 'computer', and the red Fix rows are below the Start row, off screen in a 640 px window. Start is not blocked, and the permission-granting button works before the user has agreed to anything.
findings.evidence: tagline() checks `failing` before `!onboarded`. First-run screenshot with failing checks: frdf-full.png (also frf-full.png for Linux/Wayland).
findings.fix: While not onboarded keep the first-run instruction as the tagline, and show the check count as a note by the Setup check heading. Say 'computer', and count the rows ('1 thing to fix').

findings.title: Warning-level setup rows, including “Ember can only see screenshots”, sit in a closed fold
findings.scenario: On a fresh RHEL 8 GNOME the usual state is toolkit accessibility off, which is a 'warn' row with a Turn on button. Ember's main capability (reading apps) is then reduced to screenshots, but the Setup check fold stays shut. The only hint is a small yellow '1 to look at' at the bottom of a long page. Nothing is shown in first run, because the section is hidden unless a check fails.
findings.evidence: renderChecks opens the fold and unhides the section only when `failing > 0`. Screenshot lm-open.png and linux-main-dark-full-t3.png (fold shut, '1 to look at').
findings.fix: Open the fold, or show a one-line notice under the tagline with a link to Setup, when a warn row has a fix button.

findings.title: Linux and macOS users are told Ember works "in WSL"
findings.scenario: WSL exists only on Windows, but the first-run "Before Ember starts" list ("Ember can work in WSL, on computers you reach over SSH…") and the Computers intro ("Ember can work on this computer, in WSL, and on computers you reach over SSH.") are static HTML and are never patched per OS. On RHEL and macOS the user reads about a feature that cannot exist on their machine.
findings.evidence: Dumped the real settings window's text on Linux: "Ember can work on this computer, in WSL, and on computers you reach over SSH. Your voice and your GitHub sign-in always stay here." The first-run screenshot (shots/home-first.png) shows the onboarding bullet the same way. Both strings are fixed in index.html:36 and 127 (mirrored in computers-copy.ts:14 and 24) and homePatches never touches them.
findings.fix: Add patches for #computers .intro and the onboarding li that drop "in WSL" unless platform.os is win32 (e.g. "Ember can work on this computer and on computers you reach over SSH."), and make FEATURE_TEXT skip wsl off Windows.

findings.title: First launch can show the full settings layout (sidebar, 'Checking…') before the first-run consent screen replaces it
findings.platforms: all (worse where target checks are slow, e.g. WSL or SSH rows on Windows)
findings.scenario: The settings window is shown on ready-to-show, which fires after first paint, but the first-run state (body.first-run, the Welcome card, no sidebar) is applied only when getStatus resolves. getStatus awaits the targets runtime's rows for up to 3000 ms (main.ts:359-363, waitMs:3000). Until then a brand-new user sees the post-setup page, with the sidebar, Copilot 'Checking…', Conversation, Voice and Privacy sections and the first-run tagline, which then collapses into the consent screen. A stale 'body.loading' removal remains in the code (main.ts:136 and 125), but nothing in the CSS or HTML defines that gate any more.
findings.evidence: Stubbed getStatus with a 1.5 s delay: shots/home-before-status.png shows the sidebar layout with 'Checking…' while the tagline already reads the first-run text. In real Electron, reloading the settings window and recording when body.first-run was applied: 118 ms in one run but about 1540 ms in two of three runs after cold-ish restarts (flash-real.mjs). A cold launch under Xvfb applied it within 500 ms, so the flash length depends on how long the status takes.
findings.fix: Hide the body (visibility:hidden or opacity:0) until the first status has been applied, with the existing 1.5 s timer as the cap, which is what the removed body.loading gate did. Or return the settings first and stream the slow target rows in afterwards.

findings.title: The microphone consent text is not read to a screen reader user (focus jumps straight to the “I agree” button)
findings.scenario: A screen reader user turns on 'Listen for “Hey Ember”'. The consent panel appears and focus moves to 'I agree, start listening', so the reader announces only that button. The disclosure paragraph (microphone stays open, what is sent to Copilot, 8-second follow-up) sits in a plain div before the button, so the user can press Agree without ever hearing what they agree to.
findings.evidence: index.html:92-95: #consent has no role, label or live region, and #consent-yes has no aria-describedby. main.ts:815 and 818-824 move focus to #consent-yes. Visual state: voice-consent.png (same folder).
findings.fix: Give the paragraph an id and the panel role='group' (or alertdialog) with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby to it. Put aria-describedby on #consent-yes, so the text is spoken when focus lands. Alternatively move focus to the panel (tabindex=-1) so it is read first.
